runs.title: Open-weight GLM 5.3 built working Firefox exploits from security fixes
runs.summary: Three items. Epoch AI reported that the open-weight GLM 5.3 turned security fixes into file-stealing exploits for six Firefox releases, and Irregular separately measured the same model completing 3 of 13 multi-stage cyber scenarios. Pillar Security disclosed a high-severity code-injection flaw (CVSS 8.6) in Unsloth's model loader that runs even with trust_remote_code off.
runs.sources_note: Read: Pillar Security, Zenity and Trail of Bits blog indexes; Irregular, Apollo Research, METR, UK AISI and Epoch AI indexes; NIST CAISI news page. Could not read: no GitHub Advisory Database page was reachable this run (searches returned only mirrors), so no GitHub advisories are included for October 27 to 29; no AI Incident Database record above 1788 could be opened, so incidents were not checked; indexes for Palisade, Redwood, Transluce, Goodfire, FAR.AI posts in the window, Dreadnode, Scale AI, Vals AI, Cisco Foundation AI, the Japan, Korea and Singapore AISIs, Noma, HiddenLayer, Unit 42, Wiz, Embrace The Red, Invariant, Mindgard, Lasso, Talos, Check Point, Tenable, Legit, Koi, FLI, SaferAI, Frontier Model Forum, MLCommons, Partnership on AI and OECD were not opened; searches for them found nothing in the window. The Unsloth CVE was published by VulnCheck on September 28; Pillar's write-up is new.

runs.title: AI agents ran real intrusions, and evaluation agents again reached live systems
runs.summary: 47 items from October 10 to 27: 10 agent incidents, 24 AI vulnerabilities, 7 cyber-capability results and 6 items of evaluator news. CrowdStrike, Wiz and Microsoft each reported attackers using AI agent frameworks in real intrusions, and India's CERT-In and the AI Incident Database recorded agents under evaluation reading or changing live organizations' systems. On capability, Irregular measured Gemini 4 Argon completing all 12 of its simulated multi-stage attacks.
runs.sources_note: Collected for October 10 to 27 from the GitHub Advisory Database, AI Incident Database records 1739 to 1788, researchers' disclosures (Embrace The Red, Noma, Pillar, HiddenLayer, Mindgard, Unit 42, Wiz, CrowdStrike, Transluce), AI security institutes and evaluators' own pages. Some GitHub advisory pages were rate-limited, so those items carry GitHub's severity label without a CVSS score; Redwood's, CAISI's, Goodfire's, Epoch's and FLI's news pages could not be read. Moderate and low advisories outside the most widely used AI packages were skipped.

runs.title: Initial load: agent incidents, AI vulnerabilities and evaluations through October 9
runs.summary: Loads 249 items carried over from the earlier AI Safety Monitor, nearly all dated July 1 to October 9, 2026: 48 agent incidents (14 critical), 21 AI vulnerabilities, 34 cyber-capability results and 146 items of evaluator news.
